_comment: Vendored, pinned data. Each entry: `name` (display name, matches cmpName in detection results), `detect` (how js/scripting/autodeny-snippets.generated.js recognizes the CMP at reject-action time — `global`: a window property that exists when this CMP is present; `selector`: a CSS selector for that CMP's own banner root, used as a fallback when the global isn't reliably present before the banner itself renders — kept deliberately SPECIFIC, since this same field also gates whether the CMP is considered 'detected' at all: a selector too generic risks false-positive detection on unrelated sites), `hideSelector` (OPTIONAL — the cosmetic-hide fallback's own target set, DISTINCT from `detect.selector` on purpose — see Sourcepoint's own entry for why), `action` (the FNS key in eval-snippets.js that performs the reject-all click for this CMP, or null when the CMP is recognized but only cosmetically — D12 — with no safe unattended action).
_provenance: MIXED provenance, marked per-entry via each rule's own `_source` field: `hand-authored` entries were written directly against each CMP's own public documentation/markup, confirmed via live-site Inspect-element evidence during real testing this session (design doc D2's original 'starter subset' approach). `ddg-autoconsent` entries are ADAPTED (not copy-pasted) from duckduckgo/autoconsent's own real, tested rule definitions — read directly from that project's public GitHub repo (github.com/duckduckgo/autoconsent, commit 9e4e640df401bb68c7e70d520d1174c133d20658, MPL-2.0 licensed) and translated from that project's own JSON step-sequence rule format into this project's plain-function eval-snippets.js format; simplified in places (dropping some of the upstream rule's own secondary fallback branches) rather than reproduced verbatim. `consent-o-matic` entries (added 8.4.7, two batches) are ADAPTED the same way, from cavi-au/Consent-O-Matic's own real, tested rule definitions (github.com/cavi-au/Consent-O-Matic, MIT licensed — confirmed via that repo's own LICENSE file) — read directly from their public per-CMP rule files (rules-list.json), translated from their detector/consent-toggle/save JSON schema into this project's plain-function format. Batch 1: TYPO3 Cookieman, tarteaucitron.js, Piwik PRO Consent Manager. Batch 2: GDPR Modal, Drupal EU Cookie Compliance. Batch 3: Evidon, ST CMP v2, DPDPA-style consent popup (Thai market) — all three generalized from English-text category matching to a blanket uncheck-all, avoiding language-dependency. Only entries whose action selectors were confirmed STABLE (semantic IDs/class names, generalized to attribute-prefix selectors where the naming convention allowed) were included; candidates using build-hash-dependent CSS-in-JS class names (batch 1: Admiral, Mediavine's save button; batch 2: Schibsted; batch 3: google_cwiz, whose fragility (Google's own opaque MDC classnames plus position-dependent nth-child selectors) wasn't caught by the earlier automated stability scan, found only on manual inspection) were deliberately excluded as too fragile to translate faithfully — see CHANGELOG for the full list and reasoning. None of the three categories is a fork of its respective upstream project as a whole. Batch 4 (8.4.9) draws from duckduckgo/autoconsent's own separate rules directory (334 files total, distinct from the earlier 12-entry batch's source) — fetched from the `main` branch rather than a pinned commit (GitHub's commit API was rate-limited at fetch time). 11 entries added: HubSpot, Adopt, AdRoll, Webflow, Wix, TagConcierge, Privado, Axeptio, TermsFeed, DataGrail, and Moove (direct reject-button path only — its settings-modal fallback depends on DDG's own separate EVAL_MOOVE_0 helper, not visible in the rule file itself, so dropped rather than guessed at). Two candidates deliberately deferred, not included in this batch: Transcend (DDG's own optOut action only hides the widget via CSS, never clicks an actual reject control — materially weaker than every other entry here) and Sirdata (technically stable selector, but its real value is 15+ language-specific xpath text matches — an English-only simplification would defeat the point). (11.0.0, owner's decision 2026-11-19) Both now ADDED as decline-by-hiding entries (EVAL_HIDE_ONLY, the XenForo mechanism of 10.7.16) — see their own entries. Status of the other excluded candidates in 11.0.0: Mediavine replaced its in-house CMP with consentmanager (already covered by the ConsentManager entry; scripts.mediavine.com, which loads it, is also on the Peter Lowe and HaGeZi lists); Schibsted's dialog is Sourcepoint served from its own cmp.<site> host, so js/data/cmp-loader-blocks.js's path-anchored Sourcepoint loader block applies there in decline mode (verified live 2026-11-19: vg.no loads cmp.vg.no/unified/wrapperMessagingWithoutDetection.js; NOT yet verified with the block active — Schibsted runs 'pay or okay', so the dialog may also be its content gate); Admiral's CMP ships in Admiral's one tag, which ruleset_antiadmiral and the Fox News Quick-fixes rule already stop; google_cwiz (consent.google.com) stays out — neither a loader block nor a hide fits a full-page Google consent screen.

rules.name: XenForo
rules._source: hand-authored
rules._comment: (10.7.16, owner's decision 2026-11-19) XenForo forum software's own cookie notice (verified on malwaretips.com). ALWAYS declined by hiding, in both modes: its buttons are links that navigate away and back (a click looped on malwaretips), and XenForo consent is opt-in, so an unanswered notice means essential cookies only. Decline: EVAL_HIDE_ONLY. Accept: accept.hideOnly.

rules.name: Sirdata
rules._source: adapted from ddg-autoconsent (sirdata.json) — selectors only, read 2026-11-19 from duckduckgo/autoconsent's main branch (rules/autoconsent/sirdata.json)
rules._comment: (11.0.0, owner's decision 2026-11-19) Sirdata / ABconsent CMP (France, Spain, Morocco; verified live on kotaku.com 2026-11-19: #sd-cmp present with a role=dialog, accept selector hits 'Alles accepteren', page scroll not locked, no full-screen overlay left after hiding #sd-cmp. Note: clubic.com, listed by third-party trackers as Sirdata, now uses Didomi). DECLINE by HIDING, not by blocking its loader (cache./choices.consentframework.com): AdGuard French needs an allow rule for choices.consentframework.com on frandroid.com, so blocking it breaks sites. Sirdata is an IAB TCF CMP: an unanswered dialog means no consent. Its real reject control is a localized text match (15+ languages in DDG's rule) — the reason it was deferred in 8.4.9. Accept: DDG's own opt-in button inside #sd-cmp.

rules.name: Transcend
rules._source: adapted from ddg-autoconsent (transcend.json) — selectors only, read 2026-11-19 from duckduckgo/autoconsent's main branch (rules/autoconsent/transcend.json)
rules._comment: (11.0.0, owner's decision 2026-11-19) Transcend Consent (airgap.js). DECLINE by HIDING its banner host (open shadow root) — the same as DDG's own optOut, which only hides it. NOT by blocking airgap.js: that file is Transcend's consent ENFORCER as well as the banner's loader, and sites wait on airgap.ready(). EU visitors are opted out by default, so a hidden banner means declined. Accept: DDG's own opt-in button inside the open shadow root (EVAL_ACCEPT_ALL searches it); the accept bundle hides the host afterwards, like every CMP.

rules.name: Google Funding Choices
rules._source: adapted from ddg-autoconsent (fundingchoices.json) — selectors only, read 2026-11-19 from duckduckgo/autoconsent's main branch
rules._comment: (11.0.0, owner's report 2026-11-19) Google's own consent dialog (IAB TCF). bbc.com shows it to EU visitors instead of Sourcepoint, so the Sourcepoint loader block had nothing to block there. Decline: 'Do not consent' when offered, else hidden (unanswered TCF = no consent). Accept: 'Consent'.

_comment_accept: (10.7.1) `accept` — data for EVAL_ACCEPT_ALL in eval-snippets.js, used only by the ACCEPT bundle (autoaccept-snippets.generated.js, registered while the person deletes cookies at every browser start): `api` (optional) names a documented accept-all call in that function's ACCEPT_APIS; `selectors` the CMP's own accept-all button(s), most specific first; `scope` 'document' only for a CMP whose banner is its own iframe. Empty selectors = exact-label text fallback inside the CMP's own root only. Every actionable rule has one (tools/check-autoconsent-cmp-consistency.mjs). (10.7.16) `hideOnly: true` (optional): never click this CMP, not even in the accept bundle — only hide its banner (owner's decision for XenForo: always declined).
